text:
maria: Heads-up @eng-runtime — AcmeCorp escalated after the 10:00 canary. They say function calls are either missing or getting arguments interleaved. They gave an example where a single tool call used to come back as {user_id, session_id}, now it's showing {session_id, user_id} or sometimes the tool call is omitted entirely.

kevin: Can you paste the request_id and a minimal repro? :eyes:

maria: request_id=rc-20240227-88a3. Customer sent the original prompt and model reply.
Acme: "prompt": "FetchUser(user_id=\"u-123\", session_id=\"s-456\")"
Acme: model reply (expected tool call): "CALL FetchUser {user_id:\"u-123\", session_id:\"s-456\" }"
Acme: model reply (observed): "CALL FetchUser {session_id:\"s-456\", user_id:\"u-123\" }"
Acme: or sometimes just plain text: "I couldn't find that user" without any CALL.

maria: Customer says it started right after our canary at 10:00 UTC (deploy id deploy-20240227-7).

olga: Noted. We pushed the request-mapper + batching kernel changes at 1709118000 (10:00). Could be related to batching/stream ordering or a mapper transformation. Any logs from their failing runs?

support-bot: Zendesk ticket created: ZD-98765 and linked to this thread.

maria: I captured a curl repro for them: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/respond \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-ACME' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-v1-chat","input":"FetchUser(user_id=\"u-123\", session_id=\"s-456\")","tools":[{"name":"FetchUser","params":["user_id","session_id"]}]}'
```
Expected: single tool invocation with params in order. Observed: sometimes params reversed, sometimes no tool call.

kevin: What variant/weight was the canary on? Also any downstream proxies?

maria: Canary: redwood-v1-chat@v1-quant-p3, rollout=10% traffic for canary group. Customer traffic was routed to canary bucket. No proxy on their side — direct API.

olga: Quick check: batching changes touched the streaming chunk boundaries and KV partitioning. If multiple concurrent requests share a batching slot, we may have a race that merges param buffers. Hypothesis: interleaving happening in continuous-batching path for short sequences.

kevin: Can you pull the server logs for rc-20240227-88a3 and grep for FetchUser? I want to see raw toolcall emission before the mapper. Also confirm if this is reproducible locally with same variant.

maria: Logs attached to ZD-98765. Quick repro on our side: 3/10 runs had swapped param order, 2/10 omitted tool call entirely.

dave: I can roll back the request-mapper change on the canary group immediately if we want to stop new incidents. Rollback ETA ~8-10m.

olga: While rollback is in flight, I'll push a guard that serializes param writes in the batching path to prevent buffer interleave. If that mitigates, we can then do a full patch.

kevin: Patch + rollback plan sounds good. Please post the small config change so I can apply to the hotfix branch.

olga: Patch is tiny, add this guard in serving/runtime/batcher.cc: 
```
std::scoped_lock lock(params_write_mutex);
// preserve param append order per-request
```
I'll open a PR now and kick the canary test.

maria: Customer on phone now — they're seeing a reduction but still 1/20 misses. They're ok holding while we monitor.

dave: Rollback completed on canary group at 1709123800. Traffic back to stable variant. Monitoring for 15m.

kevin: Olga's guard merged to hotfix -> deployed to canary edge at 1709123860. Running 1000 quick synthetic calls, will report back.

olga: Synthetic runs show no interleaving after guard. Looks good on p3 quant nodes.

maria: Acme confirms they no longer see missed tool calls after rollback+hotfix. They asked for postmortem and mitigation notes.

kevin: I'll draft a short postmortem and add regression tests for param ordering + end-to-end toolcall checks in CI.

maria: Thanks team — closing this loop with the customer and attaching ZD-98765 updates. :white_check_mark:
